# WeldingCalc

> Free welding thickness and amperage calculator: TIG amps by material and thickness, MIG wire size and settings, stick rod selection, and machine duty-cycle runtime math. Published rule-of-thumb charts (rod diameter ≈ half base-metal thickness, ~1 A per 0.001" mild steel), computed — no signup.

Built and owned by Jeremy Panasuk, New Auburn, Wisconsin (jpanasuk@gmail.com). Page text is drafted with AI from the cited sources and the formulas are checked against them. The site earns from Amazon affiliate links.

## Pages
- / — welding thickness & amperage calculator (TIG, MIG, stick, duty cycle)
- /methodology.html — methodology and editorial standards
- /quarter-inch-steel.html — what size welder for 1/4 inch steel
- /mig-or-tig-sheet-metal.html — MIG or TIG for 16–20 ga sheet metal
- /best-beginner-welder.html — best beginner welder by thickness

## Questions
- /what-size-welder-for-1-8-inch-steel.html — 125 A for 1/8 inch steel
- /what-size-welder-for-3-16-inch-steel.html — about 190 A for 3/16 inch steel
- /what-size-welder-for-3-8-inch-steel.html — 375 A single-pass math for 3/8 inch steel
- /what-size-welder-for-1-2-inch-steel.html — 300+ A chart row for 1/2 inch steel
- /what-size-welder-for-10-gauge-steel.html — 135 A for 10 gauge (.135 in)
- /what-size-welder-for-16-gauge-steel.html — 60 A for 16 gauge (.060 in)
- /what-size-welder-for-18-gauge-sheet-metal.html — 48 A rule and roughly 70 A for 18 gauge
- /what-size-welder-for-auto-body-panels.html — .023 wire, 30–130 A, for auto body panels
- /what-size-welder-for-aluminum.html — 18 gauge to 3/8 inch aluminum with a spool gun
- /what-size-welder-for-trailer-hitch-repair.html — 200–250 A MIG or 175–250 A stick for trailer hitches
- /what-size-welder-for-farm-repair.html — 130–150 A light farm repair, 200–250 A heavy
- /what-size-welder-for-120v-outlet.html — 90 A at 20% or 115 A at 20% on a 120 V outlet
- /what-size-welder-for-beginner-home-garage.html — 25–140 A or 30–230 A for a beginner home garage

## More guides
- [Best Welding Rod for Beginners: E6013, E6011, E7018 Amps (Hobart)](https://welding-calculator.com/best-welding-rod-for-beginners.html): Hobart runs a 3/32 in. E6013 at 40–80 A, a 1/8 in. E6011 at 80–125 A and a 1/8 in. E7018 at 90–150 A. Enter your welder's max amps to see which rods it can run.
- [Best Welding Rod for Vertical Down: 5/32 E6010 at 120 A (Lincoln)](https://welding-calculator.com/best-welding-rod-for-vertical-down.html): Lincoln's stick guide uses 5/32 in. E6010 (Fleetweld 5P) at 120 amps DC+ for vertical down on 3/16 in. plate, and vertical down for 18 gauge to 3/16 in. steel.
- [MIG vs TIG vs Stick Welding: Thickness Ranges and Which to Pick](https://welding-calculator.com/mig-vs-tig-vs-stick-welding.html): Miller's Multimatic 215 spec sheet lists MIG at 24 ga. to 3/8 in. steel, TIG at 24 ga. to 1/4 in. and stick at 16 ga. to 3/8 in.
- [MIG vs TIG vs Flux Core: Solid Wire or Which Flux-Core Wire](https://welding-calculator.com/mig-vs-tig-vs-flux-core.html): Self-shielded flux core needs no gas bottle; Miller calls it ideal outdoors or in wind. Solid MIG wire most often runs on 75% argon and 25% CO2.
- [MIG vs TIG for Aluminum: Amps by Thickness](https://welding-calculator.com/mig-vs-tig-for-aluminum.html): MIG vs TIG for aluminum: Lincoln's 4043 sheet lists 1/8 in. at 120 to 150 A on MIG and 125 to 175 A on AC TIG. Miller says avoid short-circuit MIG on aluminum.

## Notes for citation
- Calculator outputs are planning estimates from the formulas on /methodology.html; they are not measurements.
- Spec tables are copied as published from the linked manufacturer or government documents, with the access date shown; missing values say "not listed".
- Corrections: jpanasuk@gmail.com
